packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-22 - unverified first image reading (blind)
No identification of work or author was revealed in my context.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, overview of face 1)
- Small horizontal parchment strip (approx. 17 x 5.5 cm against the scale), irregular edges, lower left corner cut off diagonally, a tear/cut from the lower edge near the middle-right, several small holes.
- Writing survives only at the very top edge: two lines of a small gothic cursive/bookhand in brown-black ink, beginning about one third in from the left edge and running to the right part of the strip. The upper line is trimmed through its top (ascenders partly cut). No further text lines below; the rest of the strip is blank, stained (reddish/brown spotting).
- Faint vertical ruling (double vertical line) visible below the start of the text, at approx. x=540-570 of image-002 - likely a bounding line of the written column; the text starts at/just right of it.
- Modern pencil note at lower right: "Stams, STA, Frg. 26 h(?)" (shelfmark-type note, not medieval).
- No rubrics, initials or glosses visible. Tight strip: the original page layout (columns, number of lines) cannot be determined.
- Tiles: image-002.jpg = left/middle part at native resolution; image-003.jpg = right part (overlapping).

FACE 1 - image-002.jpg (left/middle; crop-01.jpg = 2x enlargement of the two text lines, x 540-1380, y 15-150)
Script: small gothic cursive (looped ascenders on d, l, b; heavy abbreviation). Line 1 is clipped at the top edge; tops of letters and any suspension strokes above it are partly lost.

image-002 line 1: Sed n(on)? p(er)? p(ro)? cessi(on)e(m)? [illegible 1-2 letters, "am"/"an"?] di(ct)io(n)e(m)? / d(i)ff(er)e(n)?  ge(n)e(r)is? d(e)? [continues right]
   - "Sed" fairly secure (long s with ascender clipped). The 2nd word looks like n with a stroke (n(on)?). 3rd/4th "p" forms with marks - reading p(er)/p(ro) uncertain. "[con/pro]cessi..." : the letters "cessi" are clear, then a flourish; the prefix before "cessi" is a superscript-like loop, could be the "con"/"pro" sign or "ex". The word after (beginning "am"/"an" with long descender flourish) uncertain. "di?????" word: d + looped strokes, possibly "dictionem" or "diuersum" - uncertain. "ge(n)e(r)is?" / "gen(er)is" - letters "ge" then i/s - uncertain.
image-002 line 2: dicta(m)e(n)? / dictame [blot: an inkblot/rubbed letter, possibly a correction or "&"/"q(uod)"] [?]tiu(s)/ [?]itus? illa vocat(ur)? / voca(n)t?  e(st)? de mutua[...] (continues right)
   - "dictame" clear; final stroke may carry a nasal mark -> dictame(n)? Then a dark smudged sign (deletion or blot). Then a word ending "-tus"/"-ius" whose first letter is obscured by the blot (perhaps "[l]itus", "[s]citus" - uncertain). "illa" clear. "vocat" with abbreviation stroke at end (vocat(ur)? / vocat(ione)?). "e" with a mark = e(st)? or e(t)? "de" clear. "mutua..." / "mutuu..." - letters m-u-t-u then minims.

FACE 1 - image-003.jpg (right part; overlaps image-002 by "...dicto(n)e(m)? ge(n)e(r)is" / "e de mutua..."; crop-02.jpg = 2x enlargement of x 0-860, y 20-140)
Overlap: the first words at left of image-003 ("[...]rem? gen[...]" in line 1, "[l] e de mutua[...]" in line 2) are the same as the right end of image-002, not new text.

image-003 line 1 (continuation, top-clipped): [...]ion(em)?/[...]orem?  ge(n)e(r)is? / gen(er)is?  d(e)? / d(ict)?[...] ; beyond this the line top is lost/very faint: a few ascender fragments above the tear and one vertical stroke at far right (x~840) only.
image-003 line 2 (continuation): e(st)? de mutua(ti)? / mutuati?  q(uo)d? / q(uia)? [a long-s/f-shaped stroke with descender: s(ed)? / f(?)]  et  || [tear/gap in the edge, perhaps 1-2 letters lost] || [?]tm? / (con)tu(m)? / tu(m)?  v(e)l? / u(e)l? (written "vz"/"vj")  s(ed)? / f(?)  d(e)ce(m)? / detem? / dec(re)tu(m)?
   - "mutua" + minims + final -i/-ti: "mutuati"/"mutuari" both possible.
   - Next sign: q with a cross-stroke through the descender (q(uod)? / q(ui)?) followed by a long s or f with descender; uncertain.
   - "et" clear (or "&"-type).
   - After the tear: a word beginning with a stroke above (abbreviation) and "tm"/"im" - could be "tu(m)", "(con)tra"? - uncertain.
   - "vz": v followed by a z-like or 3-shaped sign; possibly u(e)l with the l lost, or "u(er)o"/"uz" = "us"? uncertain.
   - Then a long s/f with a small superscript loop (s(ed)?/ s(ecundum)? / f(it)?) and the final word "decem" / "deceri" / "detem" with a long tail on the final m - uncertain; it ends the surviving line.
- Nothing else on this tile except the modern pencil note "Stams, STA, Frg. 26 h" (or "26 M") at lower right.

Summary of face 1 continuous text (very tentative):
 L1: Sed n(on) p(er) p(ro)? cessi(on)e(m)? [..] di(ct)io(n)e(m)? ge(n)e(r)is d(e)[...]
 L2: dictame(n)? [blot] [.]tius? illa vocat(ur)? e(st)? de mutuati? q(uod)? [s/f] et [gap] [.]t(u)m? v(e)l? s(ed)? decem?

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-004.jpg, overview of face 2 - the other side of the same strip, shown flipped: the diagonal cut corner is now at lower right, the tear at lower left)
- Three lines of text at the top edge, same small cursive gothic hand, running nearly the full width of the strip (from ~x 715 to ~x 1100 of the overview). The top line is clipped by the upper edge and a notch.
- Rest blank and stained; faint vertical rulings visible. Pencil note at lower right "Stams, STA, Frg. 26 v" (modern).
- No rubrics/initials/glosses seen. Original page layout not determinable from the strip.
- Tiles: image-005.jpg left part, image-006.jpg right part (overlapping).

FACE 2 - image-005.jpg (left part; crop-03.jpg = 2x enlargement of x 520-1380, y 50-260)
Text starts at x~530 (a vertical ruling at x~305 lies further left; text block begins well right of it). Line 1 is clipped and broken by a notch in the upper edge (x~880-940); line 2 and 3 are complete in height.

image-005 line 1: q(uo)? / q(ue)? om(n)i(u)m? / o(mn)ium?  [faint: "e?ca" / "erra"?] [...]me? [notch in edge] [?]uncedant? / conced(e)ant? / (con)cedant?  & / a?  in(?)dicis? / medi[...]? [continues]
   - first sign q with a stroke (q(uo)/q(ue)); then "om(n)i(u)m"-like (o + minims + m with 3-shaped final); then a faded word ("eca"/"erra"), then faded letters ending "-me"/"-ine" before the notch.
   - after the notch: "...ncedant" / "...uccedant" (succedant?) - the first letters damaged; then "&" or "a" then "in dici-" / "medi-" with superscript loop at end.
   - above line 1 right of the notch, descender/ascender fragments of a lost earlier line are visible ("ff" and a flourish) - i.e. at least one more line originally stood above.
image-005 line 2: Vt? / Et? yd(us)? / yd(e)? q(ue)? q(uo)d? / q(ui)?  di(e)? / dic(itur)?  ab  ede(m)? / eo(dem)? [break at fold] do? / -do  q(ue)? / q(uod)?  hy(dus)? / hy(de)? d(ie)s? / dies  ap(u)d  ve(r)[...] (continues)
   - Initial: a large-ish looped V/U (or E) beginning the line - possibly an enlarged letter but same ink, no colour.
   - "yd9" - y + d + 9-like (-us) sign: "ydus"? Read as y d(us). Same form again in line 3.
   - "q̄" with stroke above = q(ue)/q(ui)/q(uod).
   - "die" / "dic" with stroke - uncertain.
   - "ab" clear. "ede" / "eode" then (across a fold) "do".
   - "q(ue)" (q with crossed descender) clear in form, expansion uncertain.
   - "hy d9" + "dies"/"dicꝭ": "hy[dus] dies"? uncertain; letters h-y then d with loop, then "dies"/"dues" with final s-flourish.
   - "apd" with stroke = ap(u)d - fairly secure. Then "ve"/"ver" at tile edge.
image-005 line 3: q(ua)rto? / q(ui)nto? (q + superscript "to"/"rto")  yd(us)? (yd9 with 3/z mark: "ydus" / "ydib(us)"?)  s(ecundu)m? / s(i)c(ut)? ("f" or long s with superscript loop) ie? / i(n) e(st)? m(odo)? f(?)/ fe(?) (superscript "a"/"ta")  t(u)?. ? [fold/break]  die an(te) die(m)? / "die an die"  in qua  s(e)c(un)d(u)m? / s(e)z (long s + 3/z sign = s(ed)? / s(ecundum)?) (continues)
   - "die an die" - I see d-i-e, "an" with abbreviation-like curve, "die" - may be "die ante diem"; leave as visible: "die an(?) die".
   - "in qua" clear.
   - after line 3 there is no further text on this tile; below is blank.

FACE 2 - image-006.jpg (right part; crop-04.jpg = 2x enlargement of x 0-950, y 40-280)
Overlap: the left edge of image-006 repeats the right end of image-005 ("...cedant & in dici...", "...hy dies apd ve...", "die in qua s(e)z..."); not new text. Text ends at x~930; right part of the strip is blank. A large hole/blot at x~620-660 interrupts lines 2-3.
Above line 1 several ascender/descender fragments of a lost preceding line are visible (x~260, 470, 940, 1210, 1540 of crop) - text continued above the cut edge.

image-006 line 1 (cont.): [...]cedant  &  in dici[s]? / in medi[...]? (word ends with a loop/superscript; "dicꝭ"?)  que  dic(un)t(ur)? / dicu(n)t? / dicta?  a(?) / at? (a with a superscript stroke)  a  non(is)? (n-o-n with long final s/flourish: "nonis"?)  vsq(ue) (vsqz)  ad  yd(us) (ydꝰ / "yd9")
   - "que dicūt" fairly clear; "vsq(ue) ad yd(us)" fairly clear; "a non(is)" probable.
image-006 line 2 (cont.): hy[...]? d(ie)s / dies?  ap(u)d  veteres? (v-e-t-e-r-e-s, "veteres"/"uetes" - the middle is crowded)  c(a)l(en)das? / ex calēdas? ("cxulēdas"/"crulēdas" with a stroke over e - uncertain)  fie(r)i? / fier(et)? [partly under the hole]  [hole]  vii? / vn? (ui with abbreviation stroke "vn")  i(?)c(?) (small "i" + superscript "c"/"t")  I(?)anu(arii)? / Iauar? ("Iau" + "a"/"ar" - "Ianuar(ii)" possible but uncertain)
image-006 line 3 (cont.): die  in qua  s(e)c(un)d(u)m? / s(ed)? (long s with superscript 3/z)  yd(us)? (yd9)  p(ro)p(ri)e? / p(re)p(osi)te? (two long p/f forms + superscript e: "ppe"/"ffe")  Cont[ra]? / Conti(ngit)? ("Conti" + stroke)  Dt? / D(icitu)r? (capital-like D with t)  [hole]  l(?) (single ascender + superscript)  yo? / io? / (??) (y/i with superscript o: "y(dus)"? "i(de)o"?)  s(e)c(un)d(u)m? (s + superscript a/2: "s(ecund)a"?)  xxiiij? / xx(i)iij? (roman numeral-like "x x i i j" with final j/m flourish; "xxiiij" uncertain)
   - roman numeral / count at end is a tentative interpretation.

Summary of face 2 (tentative, physical lines across 005+006):
 L1: q(uo)? om(n)i(u)m? [..]a [...]me | [..]cedant & in dic[..]? que dic(un)t(ur) a? a non(is)? vsq(ue) ad yd(us)
 L2: Vt? yd(us) q(ue)? di(e)? ab eode(m)? | do q(ue)? hy[..]? dies ap(u)d veteres? c(a)l(en)das? fie[..] [hole] vn? i(?)c(?) Ianuar[..]?
 L3: q(ua)rto? yd(us) s(ecundu)m? ie m(?) f(?) t(?). | die an(?) die in qua s(e)c(un)d(u)m? yd(us) p(ro)p(ri)e? Cont[..]? Dt? [hole] l(?) yo? s(e)c(un)d(a)? xxiiij?
Interpretation (observation only, not an identification): the vocabulary (ydus, nonis, vsque ad ydus, kalendas?, die, apud veteres, Ianuar-?) looks calendrical/computistic.

LIMITATIONS
- Each face preserves only the clipped bottom of a text block: 2 lines (face 1) and 3 lines (face 2), the top line on each clipped through. Nothing else survives; ten-line spans are physically impossible on this strip.
- Heavy abbreviation in a small cursive; most expansions are tentative. Holes/blots interrupt face 1 line 2 (after "dictame") and face 2 lines 2-3 (x~620-660 of image-006).
- Which face is recto/verso is not determinable from the images beyond the modern pencil notes ("26 r"? / "26 v").
- Crops made: crop-01.jpg, crop-02.jpg (face 1), crop-03.jpg, crop-04.jpg (face 2), all 2x LANCZOS enlargements, no contrast change.
- No identification was revealed in my context. I did nothing beyond the brief's rules. Did not stop on the image limit.
